items.name: MBC_MIN_BANDS

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed include/omxdsp/fx/omx_mbcomp.h:56 #define OMX_MBC_MIN_BANDS 2u, staged there until this declaration: omx_mbcomp_design and omx_mbcomp_process refuse a band count below it (PRE band-count-declared)

items.doc: The fewest bands the multiband compressor splits into: one crossover. omx_mbcomp_design and omx_mbcomp_process refuse a band count below it (`band-count-declared`), and a refused count reads as this floor.

items.name: MBC_MAX_BANDS

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed include/omxdsp/fx/omx_mbcomp.h:60 #define OMX_MBC_MAX_BANDS 5u, staged there until this declaration: the band count's ceiling and the extent of the stage's inline state

items.doc: The most bands the multiband compressor splits into, and the capacity of its inline state: `struct omx_mbcomp_state` holds this many band compressors and one crossover fewer per leg, so the ceiling and the arrays are one fact.

items.name: MBC_CORNER_MAX_FRACTION

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed include/omxdsp/fx/omx_mbcomp.h:64 #define OMX_MBC_CORNER_MAX_FRACTION 0.45, staged there until this declaration, read as a double at omx_mbcomp_design (top = fraction x sr)

items.doc: The highest crossover corner the multiband design builds, as a fraction of the live rate: a corner at or above `fraction x rate` is designed AT that line, because the LR4 section degenerates toward Nyquist. omx_mbcomp_design computes the line in double, so a C reader takes OMX_MBC_CORNER_MAX_FRACTION_DOUBLE. A 20 kHz corner is under the line from 48 kHz up; at 44.1 kHz the line is 19845 Hz and a 20 kHz corner is designed there.
